polycarp-of-smyrna: His held words are one letter, to Philippi. The rule for Alexander of Alexandria and Ossius (era 2 batch 5) leaves that short of major. Ignatius carries this tradition's early bishops.
irenaeus-of-lyon: His five books Against Heresies are the fullest answer to the Valentinians we have, like Epiphanius's catalogue (era 2 batch 3).
tertullian-s-voice: The first major Christian author in Latin. He made the words the West argued in: trinitas, persona, substantia.
origen: The scholar of the early church, who wrote on almost every book of the Bible. Later quarrels turned on his work, as the batch entries for Epiphanius and Evagrius record.
cyprian-of-carthage: He led the church of Carthage through persecution and schism. His letters are the fullest record of how a third-century church was run.
pamphilus-of-caesarea: A keeper and copyist of Origen's books, known mainly through Eusebius. This follows the recorders in the batches.
lactantius: Tertullian is the larger Latin apologist. The same rule kept Aetius under Eunomius (era 2 batch 2).
methodius-of-olympus: A bishop who wrote the Banquet and wrote against Origen. He founded no tradition and drove no council.
constantine-the-great: He ended the ban on the church and called the bishops to Nicaea. That is the council-driver rule used for Cyril of Alexandria (era 2 batch 5).
athanasius-of-alexandria: Bishop of Alexandria for forty-five years, the defender of Nicaea. The era 2 batch 5 entry says he carries the river.
ephrem-the-syrian: He taught the faith in hymns the whole congregation sang. He is the leading voice of Syriac Edessa in this era.
basil-of-caesarea: His On the Holy Spirit answered those who ranked the Spirit lower, and his rule governed later monasteries.
ambrose-of-milan: Bishop of Milan for twenty-three years, who told emperors where their power stopped. His tradition is named after him.
gregory-of-nazianzus: His Five Theological Orations on the Trinity won him the title 'the Theologian'.
gregory-of-nyssa: Basil and Gregory of Nazianzus carry the Cappadocians. His named works finish Basil's reply to Eunomius and tell Macrina's life. This is the Aetius precedent again.
paula-of-rome: She led the women's community at Bethlehem. Jerome carries the Bethlehem Circle, and her life is known through his letters.
jovinian: Condemned at Rome and Milan and known mainly through Jerome's answer. He founded no tradition.
jerome: He put the Old Testament into Latin from the Hebrew, in the work later called the Vulgate.
augustine-of-hippo: The most fully recorded pastor of the ancient world. He was priest and bishop of Hippo until 430.
john-chrysostom: The great preacher of Antioch and Constantinople, exiled for preaching against the court.
nestorius: The controversy took his name. He was deposed at Ephesus in 431, and the Church of the East kept his defense. This is the rule that made Eutyches major (era 2 batch 6).
patrick-of-ireland: Irish and Welsh writers place him at the start of their story. That is the founder rule used for Frumentius (era 2 batch 1).
peter-the-iberian: He led the people near Gaza who refused Chalcedon. He is known through John Rufus's Life, and he founded no tradition.
simeon-of-beth-arsham: Known for one letter on the martyrs of Najran. Philoxenus and Severus carry the Syriac Orthodox river.
justinian-i: He wrote church law and called the council of 553, which is the council-driver rule.
gregory-the-great: Bishop of Rome from 590. The Latin West read his Pastoral Rule, Moralia and Dialogues for centuries.
heraclius: The Ecthesis went out in his name, but Sergius's synod made it. The rule for emperors is calling or driving a council, as Constantine and Justinian did.
gregory-vii: He cut Henry IV off from the church in 1076. His Register claims that a pope may depose emperors.
innocent-iii: His Fourth Lateran Council made law for the whole Latin church.
bonaventure: He led the Franciscans and wrote their standard Life of Francis. The Franciscan tradition grew from Francis, not from him.
martin-luther: He would not take back his books before the emperor, and he put the Bible into German. Wittenberg's reform is his.
william-tyndale: He put the New Testament into English. His entry calls him a forerunner who stands before the English Reformation.
john-calvin: The author of the Institutes and Geneva's reformer.
ignatius-of-loyola: He founded the Society of Jesus.
hugo-grotius: A jurist who sided with the Remonstrants. The tradition was not his to lead.
john-wesley: Methodism grew from his open-air preaching, which his fifty-five-year journal records.
